description:
We are AIUB XENOBLADE, a team from the American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB), Dhaka, Bangladesh 

🌎 Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

Our project aims to make Martian accessible through an immersive 3D Mars globe, terrain   and a Mission Lab by NASA-related datasets.

By transforming planetary data into an interactive exploration experience, we aim to help students, researchers, space enthusiasts, and future explorers better understand the Martian environment.
summary: MARS // SURVIVE is our NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 project for “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.” It is a browser-based Mars exploration and mission-planning platform built with React, TypeScript, TanStack Router, Three.js, and React Three Fiber. Its routes cover a planetary map, hazard analysis, resource explorer, mission lab, Mars clock and compass, terrain/AI lab, team page, Sol-by-Sol life-support simulator, and rover expedition. The map combines NASA Mars Trek WMTS imagery and layers with location selection, telemetry, measurement, waypoints, and safest/fastest/science-oriented graph-route options. The hazard module computes a weighted multi-component MERI risk score with mobility modes and veto conditions. Resource and terrain context includes a local MOLA-style topography grid, regional SWIM-inspired ice benchmarks, and a bundled 128×128 Jezero elevation patch. The Sol-by-Sol simulator is a separate static application; a quick simulator offers sensitivity controls for crew, duration, water, power, shielding, and dust. NASA Image Library search is available in the map, while Hugging Face inference and Google Gemini advisor calls are optional server integrations requiring credentials. Regional 3D assets and a standalone six-wheel rover simulation are included. The NASA Data Atlas catalogs sources and analogs; it does not mean every listed archive is downloaded or processed live. Outputs are educational prototypes, not operational or NASA-certified advice.
details: MARS // SURVIVE is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.” It combines planetary mapping, hazard context, resource-planning tools, Mars timekeeping, and a browser-based rover experience. The application uses a React and TypeScript frontend, TanStack routing, Three.js/WebGL visualizations, NASA Mars Trek map tiles, and NASA’s image library API. Features include a 2D/3D planetary map, terrain and location telemetry, selectable hazard layers, Mars clock and compass, mission-planning tools, an interactive survival simulator, a Jezero terrain demonstration, and rover driving controls. Optional AI features support image analysis and a Mars-advisor workflow. Some planetary context is supplied by bundled reference grids and regional benchmark values; not all referenced NASA archives are loaded live. Model outputs are exploratory and are not NASA-certified or intended for real mission decisions.
